Subject: PilotRetail — vector alignment & auth next steps

Hi Evan / Lydia,

Thanks again for the call today — helpful to get a clearer picture of PilotRetail's search and recommendations flow. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the open technical items so we can align engineering work on both sides. Short version up top, details and asks below.

TL;DR / next steps (owners):
- Confirm target vector dimension and normalization strategy (PilotRetail) — Evan (answer by 4/28)
- Provide sample export of ~5k vectors and the metadata schema (PilotRetail) — Lydia (upload to Drive)
- Redwood to propose batching/settings for expected QPS and average doc token length (Karthik) — deliver 4/27
- Decide auth model: API key vs AWS IAM role with STS (PilotRetail + Redwood) — sync by 4/30
- Migration path from current provider (you mentioned Pinecone) — Ben to draft stepwise plan (Ben)

Detailed items / clarifying questions:
1) Vector dimensions and normalization
- You mentioned current vectors are 1536-d from the service you use today. Are all artifacts already at 1536 or do you have some legacy 1024 assets? If mixed, do you plan to re-embed everything or maintain multiple indexes?
- For semantic search quality, do you currently L2-normalize vectors before upsert? If so, is that done client-side in your pipeline or by the vector store?

2) Batching and traffic profile
- What sustained QPS should we optimize for and what are peak bursts (per-minute)?
- Average and 95th percentile document lengths (tokens) for text that gets embedded. This informs batch sizing and latency tradeoffs in Redwood's runtime.

3) Migration and consistency
- How critical is zero-downtime during migration? Can you tolerate a short dual-write window?
- Do you store versioned vector ids or rely on external doc ids?

4) Auth and network
- Two recommended patterns: 1) API keys scoped to the project + IP allowlist (fast, self-serve); 2) AWS IAM (AssumeRole via STS) for private deployment and S3/KMS integration (preferred for stricter controls). Any constraints?

Attachments: I attached a quick integration diagram and an auth checklist template (see attachments). Also including a snippet below for how the Redwood SDK handles upserts and a sample reranker call that uses structured tool-calling style metadata.

--- code snippet (JS) ---
// upsert (pseudo)
await redwood.vectors.upsert({
  index: 'pilot_products',
  vectors: [
    { id: 'sku_123', values: [...], metadata: { category: 'footwear', price: 79.99 } }
  ],
  normalize: true, // client-side flag, Redwood runtime also supports server normalization
  batchSize: 256
});

// rerank (pseudo)
const rerank = await redwood.reranker.score({
  model: 'redwood-rerank-v1',
  query: 'waterproof hiking shoes',
  candidates: ['sku_123','sku_456'],
  returnStructured: true // returns {score, toolCalls: [...] } for deterministic downstream routing
});

Subject: Re: PilotRetail — vector alignment & auth next steps

Hi Karthik — thanks for the tidy recap. A few answers inline.

1) Vector dims: yes, we're currently at 1536 across the board — legacy 1024 embeddings were retired last quarter. We'll send a sample export (5k) by EOD tomorrow; Lydia will upload. We normalize vectors on our side (client), so upserts are already L2-normalized.

2) Traffic: baseline QPS is ~18 sustained; peak bursts hit ~220 QPS during promotions (short spikes lasting 10–20 minutes). Average document length for embedding is about 600 tokens; 95th percentile around 1,800.

3) Migration: we prefer a dual-write approach for a 48-hour window, with read-traffic slowly shifting once verification passes. We store external doc ids (sku or product id) and version them in metadata. Zero downtime is nice-to-have but not mandatory.

4) Auth: security prefers IAM for long-term, but initial POC can use scoped API keys. We will need IP allowlisting for the POC too.

Uploading: Lydia will upload the export + schema to the Drive link you shared. Evan

--

Nice — solid answers Evan, thanks. Internal notes / next steps for us:
- Karthik: draft recommended batching config for 18 QPS sustained, 220 burst. Prioritize median batch size for 600-token docs but include fallback for 1,800-token cases. Deliver by 4/27.
- Ben: draft migration playbook. Include verification checks (cosine similarity sampling, top-k consistency test) and rollback criteria. Start w/ 48-hour dual-write plan and list team touchpoints (PilotRetail engineering, our infra ops). Deliver initial doc by 4/29.
- Marissa: I'll coordinate procurement timeline and share contract CLM link with PilotRetail (they asked about SSO/KMS in their enterprise package).

Evan / Lydia: a couple of asks to help our runbook:
- Upload the 5k vector export + schema to the Drive folder and confirm whether you have client-side dedupe across ids.
- Share a rough timetable for when procurement (legal + security) ramps — helps us pick the auth path (API key POC vs IAM planning).

I'll spin up a shared checklist in the Drive folder and link to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks team — starting the migration playbook now. A few immediate technical checkpoints I'm adding:
- Upsert id strategy: ensure PilotRetail's sku/product ids are immutable or include version metadata. If ids can be reused, we'll recommend a composite id (sku + embedding_version).
- Consistency test: after dual-write, we'll sample 1k items, compute top-10 nearest on both systems and measure agreement (>= 92% top-10 overlap target).
- Cost estimate: include incremental token and storage cost for keeping both systems for 48 hours.
- Rollback: keep read-traffic on legacy for 24 hours after initial switch; auto-route to legacy on >5% degradation in CTR or retrieval accuracy.

I'll produce an initial doc and attach it to the Drive folder (will also include a lightweight migration checklist as a CSV). Ben
